title: Artin–Schreier character sheaves over arbitrary finite rings are flat lisse lines
statement: Let $p$ be a prime, let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring in which $p$ is a unit, and let $X$ be a scheme with $p=0$ in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ (the empty scheme is allowed). Let $b\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and let $\Psi:(\mathbf F_p,+)\to\Lambda^\times$ be an additive character. Form the Artin–Schreier sheaf $L=\mathcal L_{\Psi,b}$ of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] (current general-coefficient statement), with finite field $\mathbf F_p$: explicitly, for the covering $q:Y=\operatorname{Spec}_X(\mathcal O_X[T]/(T^p-T-b))\to X$, it is the image of the idempotent $p^{-1}\sum_{a\in\mathbf F_p}\Psi(-a)\sigma_a$ on $q_*\Lambda_Y$, where $\sigma_a$ acts by pullback along $T\mapsto T+a$. All sheaves are sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules on the small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Then $q$ is a finite étale surjective morphism, $q^{-1}L\cong\Lambda_Y$, and $L$ is étale locally free of rank one as a $\Lambda_X$-module. In particular $L$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] and flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. No nontriviality of $\Psi$, finite-type hypothesis on $X$, or assumption that $\Lambda$ is a field or local ring is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A3J, section-artin-schreier, exact Artin–Schreier sequence; character-idempotent trivialization as in the argument recorded in report.md

proof.text: On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$, the prescribed relative spectrum is $q^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, where $B=A[T]/(T^p-T-b|_U)$. The relation $T^p=T+b|_U$ reduces every power to an $A$-linear combination of $1,T,\ldots,T^{p-1}$, by induction on its degree. Thus $B$ is a finite $A$-module and $q$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The polynomial is monic and its derivative is $-1$, since $p=0$ in $A$. Consequently $B=A[T]_{-1}/(T^p-T-b|_U)$ is the standard étale algebra of [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative], so its spectrum is étale over $U$. These affine charts cover $X$ and their inverse images cover $Y$, hence $q$ is étale by the affine-local characterization in [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Tags 00UB (definition-standard-etale) and 00UC (lemma-standard-etale), clause (1); monic reduction and affine-local finiteness

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-artin-schreier-polynomial-cover] with $U=X$ and $t=b$. It gives an étale surjection $f:V\to X$ and $\omega\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ with $\omega^p-\omega=f^*b$. For every affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ and every affine open $W\subset f^{-1}U$, the ring map $A[T]/(T^p-T-b|_U)\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_V)$ sending $T$ to $\omega|_W$ defines a spectrum map $W\to q^{-1}U$; these maps agree on overlaps because they have the same base map and the same image of $T$. They glue to $h:V\to Y$ with $qh=f$. Every point of $X$ therefore lies in the image of $q$. This proves surjectivity, also when $X$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0A3J (section-artin-schreier), local solvability of T^p-T=b, followed by the explicit factorization through the specified covering

proof.text: Set $A=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_p[x]$, $D=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_p[u]$ and $\alpha:D\to A$, $x\mapsto u^p-u$. Write $t$ for the universal root on $Y$ and let $h:Y\to D$ send $u$ to $t$. Then $\alpha h=bq$. This square is cartesian: for maps $s:Z\to X$ and $v:Z\to D$ with $bs=\alpha v$, the function $v^*u$ satisfies $(v^*u)^p-v^*u=s^*b$. On each affine $W\subset s^{-1}(U)$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$, there is the unique ring map $R[T]/(T^p-T-b|_U)\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_Z)$ sending $T$ to $v^*u|_W$. These maps glue uniquely since the base map and root agree on overlaps. They give the unique $Z\to Y$ over $X$ with composite $h$ equal to $v$, exactly [def-pc-fibre-product]. For $X=A$, $b=x$, this construction identifies the relative cover with $D$: the inverse ring maps send $(x,T)$ to $(u^p-u,u)$ and $u$ to $T$. Thus step 1 also proves that $\alpha$ is finite étale. The maps $\tau_a:D\to D$, $u\mapsto u+a$, and $\sigma_a:Y\to Y$, $t\mapsto t+a$, satisfy $h\sigma_a=\tau_a h$, since both pull back $u$ to $t+a$.

source.place: AS_p and pullback along b; explicit universal-property verification for the equation T^p-T=b

proof.text:
Put $M=\mathcal L_\Psi=\operatorname{im}(e_\Psi\mid\alpha_*\Lambda_D)$ on $A$, so the current definition in the statement gives $L=b^{-1}M$. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] to the cartesian square $(h,q,\alpha,b)$ of step 3, with $\alpha$ finite and with the underlying abelian sheaf of $\Lambda_D$. It makes the underived exchange an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear] to this same square, coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and module sheaf $\Lambda_D$: the very same exchange map is $\Lambda_X$-linear. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](1),(2), $h^{-1}\Lambda_D\cong\Lambda_Y$ as constant module sheaves. Consequently these maps give a module-sheaf isomorphism
$$\beta:b^{-1}\alpha_*\Lambda_D\xrightarrow{\sim}q_*\Lambda_Y.$$
Indeed the inverse of a bijective module map is linear: if $\beta(z)=w$, then $\beta(\lambda z)=\lambda w$, whence $\beta^{-1}(\lambda w)=\lambda\beta^{-1}(w)$. No module base-change assertion is inferred solely from abelian invertibility, and only the underived finite-exchange clause is used.

source.place: Tag 0959, lemma-finite-pushforward-commutes-with-base-change; module linearity supplied by the cited existing node (Stacks 03S6 exchange on modules)

proof.text:
The isomorphism $\beta$ intertwines the translations, as follows from the section formula in [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]. For $V\to X$ étale, take a representative consisting of $W\to A$ étale, $V\to W\times_AX$ and a section $s$ of $\Lambda_D$ on $D\times_AW$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], view $s$ as a locally constant $\Lambda$-valued function. Its image is pullback along $\kappa:Y\times_XV\to D\times_AW$, $(y,z)\mapsto(h(y),w(z))$, with $w:V\to W$ the given map, followed by sheafification. Step 3 gives
$$\kappa\circ(\sigma_a\times\mathrm{id}_V)=(\tau_a\times\mathrm{id}_W)\circ\kappa.$$
Hence $(s\circ(\tau_a\times\mathrm{id}_W))\circ\kappa=(s\circ\kappa)\circ(\sigma_a\times\mathrm{id}_V)$. This identity persists under restriction and sheafification, proving $\beta\circ b^{-1}(\tau_a^*)=\sigma_a^*\circ\beta$. Since $\beta$ is linear, it therefore intertwines $b^{-1}e_\Psi$ and $e^Y_\Psi=p^{-1}\sum_a\Psi(-a)\sigma_a^*$. Exactness of $b^{-1}$ from [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3) preserves images. Thus $L=b^{-1}M$ is canonically isomorphic to $\operatorname{im}(e^Y_\Psi\mid q_*\Lambda_Y)$, with its inclusion identified by $\beta$. This proves the statement's 'explicitly' clause for the sheaf defined by pullback, before computing $q^{-1}L$.

source.place: Tag 0959, canonical exchange; section-restriction formula of def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange and Tag 03P5, remark-constant-locally-constant-maps

proof.text: Write $t$ for the universal root on $Y$, and $t_1,t_2$ for its two pullbacks to $Z=Y\times_XY$. The characteristic-$p$ binomial identity gives $(t_2-t_1)^p-(t_2-t_1)=0$. At every point $z$ of $Z$, its local ring has $p=0$, so [lem-sc-local-ring-artin-schreier-kernel] gives a unique $a\in\mathbf F_p$ with $(t_2-t_1)_z=a$. Equality of germs holds on an open neighbourhood of $z$. Hence the loci $Z_a$ on which $t_2-t_1=a$ form a disjoint open partition of $Z$. The translation $t\mapsto t+a$ defines $s_a:Y\to Z$, $y\mapsto(y,\sigma_a y)$, since $(t+a)^p-(t+a)=b$. Its image lies in $Z_a$. Conversely, on $Z_a$ the two coordinates satisfy $t_2=t_1+a$, so the presentation by the universal root implies $s_a\operatorname{pr}_1=\mathrm{id}_{Z_a}$, while $\operatorname{pr}_1s_a=\mathrm{id}_Y$. Thus these actual inverse maps give $Z\cong\coprod_{a\in\mathbf F_p}Y$ over the first projection. There are no points or loci to check when $Y$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0A3J (section-artin-schreier), kernel equal to the constant F_p; explicit root-difference trivialization

proof.text: Because $q$ is étale, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identifies inverse image with restriction: for $V\to Y$ étale, $(q^{-1}q_*\Lambda_Y)(V)=(q_*\Lambda_Y)(V\to X)=\Lambda_Y(V\times_XY)$, the last equality being [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Step 6 identifies $V\times_XY$ with $\coprod_{a\in\mathbf F_p}V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], sections of the constant sheaf are Zariski-locally constant functions; on this disjoint union they are tuples $(f_a)_{a\in\mathbf F_p}$ with $f_a\in\Lambda_V(V)$. This gives $q^{-1}q_*\Lambda_Y\cong\prod_{a\in\mathbf F_p}\Lambda_Y$, naturally in $V$. Naturality of the restriction comparison and the constant-ring comparison in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] make this an isomorphism of $\Lambda_Y$-modules. Pullback along translation by $c$ sends the tuple to $(f_{a+c})_a$: it changes the second root from $t+a$ to $t+a+c$.

source.place: Tag 03S2 (section-extension-by-zero), restriction description of étale inverse image; Tag 03P5 (remark-constant-locally-constant-maps)

proof.text:
Using the identification of $L$ proved in step 5, exactness of the module inverse image in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies $q^{-1}L$ with the image of the pulled-back projector on the product in step 7. For a tuple $f=(f_a)$ of sections, put $c(f)=p^{-1}\sum_{d\in\mathbf F_p}\Psi(-d)f_d$. Reindexing $d=a+r$ gives
$$ (e_\Psi f)_r=p^{-1}\sum_a\Psi(-a)f_{r+a}=\Psi(r)c(f). $$
Define $g_r=\Psi(r)$. Then $c(g)=p^{-1}\sum_d1=1$, so $e_\Psi(g\lambda)=g\lambda$ for any section $\lambda$ of $\Lambda_Y$. Thus the image is exactly $\{g\lambda\}$; multiplication by $g$ is an isomorphism from $\Lambda_Y$ to that image, with inverse evaluation at $r=0$, since $\Psi(0)=1$. All formulas commute with restriction, hence define an isomorphism of sheaves $q^{-1}L\cong\Lambda_Y$. No cancellation by a nonunit or character orthogonality is used. The same calculation works for the trivial character and the zero coefficient ring.

source.place: Character projector e_Psi; explicit regular-representation computation over an arbitrary commutative coefficient ring

proof.text: Steps 1, 2 and 8 provide the singleton étale cover $q:Y\to X$ on which $L$ is the free module $\Lambda_Y$ of rank one. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], $q^{-1}L$ is the restriction $L|_Y$, so this is a trivializing datum. Thus $L$ is étale locally free of rank one, and locally constant in the sense of [def-constructible-locally-constant]. Since $\Lambda$ is finite, this is a finite locally constant module sheaf. For [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] take the one-stratum partition $X$ with its identity immersion: its image is constructible (the whole space is open and is retrocompact in itself), and the required finite locally constant restriction is $L$ itself. If $X$ is empty, use the empty partition. This proves constructibility without any Noetherian or finite-type condition on $X$.

source.place: Tag 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant); Tag 095E (lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), condition (3) used as the recorded global definition

proof.text: Let $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$ be any short exact sequence of $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves. Restriction to $Y$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The localization equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open], together with [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], identifies this with restriction to the slice site $X_{\Et}/Y$. By [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction], the restriction of the sequence tensored with $L$ is the restricted sequence tensored with $L|_Y\cong\Lambda_Y$ (step 8), hence is the original restricted exact sequence: the mutually inverse unit maps are $x\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda x$ and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Exactness therefore holds on this covering. Explicitly the kernel, cokernel and middle homology sheaves of the tensored sequence restrict to zero, since restriction is exact. For any étale $W\to X$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] gives the cover $W\times_XY\to W$; a section of any of these defect sheaves is zero on that cover, so is zero by the separatedness axiom for a sheaf. All three defects vanish globally. Thus tensoring with $L$ is exact, which is flatness as defined in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

source.place: Tags 03DH (section-localize), 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), 03ER (definition-flat), item (3); exactness detected by the sheaf axiom on a cover
